content.thinking:
I'm tracing the causal chain from the symptom—account pages failing for shoppers—back through the error logs to find the root cause, citing the relevant evidence sources as I go. The trail leads to a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py, caused by a deploy that changed filtering logic so accounts with no purchases this month end up dividing by zero.

The exposure traces to a monthly-spend-feature flag ramp: when the flag was off errors dropped to 58 from 142, and the flag revert is confirmed as the fix, but since the deploy rollback was never actually performed, I can't be fully certain whether the deploy alone or the flag ramp is the sole root cause—I should flag this ambiguity in my conclusions and note the missing zero-guard as a contributing factor, proposing action items for a regression test and for fixing the unreachable rollback path.

Detection was also delayed by several minutes after the issue began, which deserves its own action item, and I want to recommend that flag ramps never happen simultaneously with deploys going forward. I'll lay out AI-3 through AI-6 covering the regression test, the rollback path, the detection delay, and the deploy/flag-ramp separation process, while being careful not to restate specific numeric figures when describing the detection gap or flag counts.

action_items.item: Add a regression test for the spend summary with an account that has no purchases in the current month, and guard the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. Include it in the fix PR.
Require that a feature flag ramp for newly deployed code starts at a small share of traffic and does not begin in the same minute as the deploy. Ramp only after the error rate is checked.
Investigate why the deployment platform was unreachable to Argus during the incident, and add a fallback path or an alert so that rollback is available when needed.
Add a faster alert on the account page error rate, or on the ZeroDivisionError log signature, so a regression at deploy time is paged within the first minute or so rather than several minutes later.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw account page requests fail. The error rate went from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}, starting at the onset {began} and recovering at {recovered}.
The failing requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. This was a code exception, not a client disconnect or a platform problem.

The spend summary divides the monthly total by the count of purchases in the current month. Accounts with no purchases this month make the divisor zero. The revision deployed at the onset changed this code to filter by recorded_at, and the Investigator identified that change as the source of the unguarded division. I could not check this against the diff itself.
The new path was exercised as the monthly-spend-feature flag was ramped. It was partly on at the onset and fully on afterwards, and errors persisted while it was on.

Reverting the flag to off stopped the errors and the service returned to baseline. That confirms the flag-gated path was where the failure happened. The deployment rollback never ran, so the code defect remains in the deployed revision.

contributing_factors.factor: The zero-purchases case was not covered by tests or review. The change shipped with an unguarded division on a count that can be empty.

The flag ramp happened in the same minute as the deploy, so a new code path and its exposure changed together. This made the cause ambiguous, and nothing limited the exposure of the new code to a small slice of traffic first.
The deployment platform could not be reached, so the preferred mitigation, a rollback, was unavailable. The flag revert was the only lever that worked.
The alert was raised several minutes after the errors began, so most of the impact had passed before a response started.

input.executive_summary: For {duration}, a share of shoppers could not load their account pages on io-shop. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. It began the minute a new revision was deployed and a new monthly-spend feature was ramped up. The automated response tried to roll back the deployment but the deployment platform could not be reached. It then switched the feature flag off, and errors returned to baseline. The flag remains off and a draft fix is awaiting review. The underlying code defect is still in production, hidden behind the flag.

got_lucky: The faulty path sat behind a feature flag, so switching it off was enough to stop the errors even though the rollback was unavailable.
Re-enabling the flag before the fix merges would bring the failure back. Nothing in the record prevents that.
went_well: Argus gave a hypothesis quickly, and when the rollback failed it moved straight to the flag revert without delay.
The flag revert was confirmed against the metrics before the incident was marked mitigated.
A draft fix pull request was proposed right after mitigation.
went_wrong: The leading candidate, a deploy rollback, could not be carried out because the platform was unreachable.
The alert fired several minutes after onset.
The defect is still in the deployed code and is hidden only by the flag being off.

input.root_cause: A deployed change to the monthly spend summary computed an average by dividing by the number of purchases in the current month without guarding against zero. Once the monthly-spend-feature flag sent traffic down that path, account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month raised ZeroDivisionError.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
